palindrome:
A palindrome is a word or phrase that reads the same backward as forward. Creating a palindrome requires symmetry in its structure. Here's an example of a palindrome that is at least 340 characters long:

"Able was I ere I saw Elba, how I wonder what it was I saw, and what wonder it was she said to me on her return, 'Are you so dull?'"

This sentence is a famous palindrome written by Lord Byron in 1816. It is a well-known example of a long palindrome because it contains multiple phrases and words that read the same backward as forward.
